title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CLIFF'S ROWBOAT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Cliff Hartsell, an auctioneer from Paducah, Kentucky.
Forty years ago, he promised his wife Darlene a boat. Built with his own two hands. He never built it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: ONE BOARD
segments.quote: The creation of a thousand forests is in one acorn.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: Their fortieth anniversary was one summer away. Cliff had never built so much as a birdhouse.
At an estate sale, an old book fell open to a line from Ralph Waldo Emerson:
The creation of a thousand forests is in one acorn.
So Cliff bought one cedar board and leaned it in his garage.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TWO HUNDRED STEPS
segments.quote: Our grand business undoubtedly is, not to see what lies dimly at a distance, but to do what lies clearly at hand.
segments.author: Thomas Carlyle
lines: The rowboat plans came in the mail. Two hundred steps.
Cliff stared at page one for a week. So Darlene taped up a line from Thomas Carlyle, a Scottish writer:
Our grand business undoubtedly is, not to see what lies dimly at a distance, but to do what lies clearly at hand.
He stopped worrying about step two hundred, and cut piece number one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: OLD MR. PATE
segments.quote: To be conscious that you are ignorant is a great step to knowledge.
segments.author: Benjamin Disraeli
lines: By August, he had split three boards and one thumbnail.
Down the street lived Rufus Pate, eighty-two, who built wooden boats for fifty years. Cliff was too proud to ask.
Then he remembered Benjamin Disraeli, the British statesman:
To be conscious that you are ignorant is a great step to knowledge.
So he knocked and said, I don't know what I'm doing. Rufus grinned. Finally, an honest auctioneer.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: STICKY
segments.quote: Slow and steady wins the race.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: By fall, Cliff got cocky. Three coats of varnish in one cold night.
By morning, the boat was sticky as a pancake. Rufus quoted Aesop:
Slow and steady wins the race.
So Cliff sanded it all off. One thin coat a day, all winter.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: LAUNCH DAY
segments.quote: There is no disgrace in honest failure; there is disgrace in fearing to fail.
segments.author: Henry Ford
lines: In June, half the street came to Kentucky Lake for the launch.
Cliff pushed off. Water came in around his boots.
He wanted to hide. Then Rufus called out a line from Henry Ford:
There is no disgrace in honest failure; there is disgrace in fearing to fail.
Cliff bailed with his hat, laughed, fixed one bad seam, and launched again. She floated.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: FORTY YEARS
segments.quote: Marriage is one long conversation, checkered by disputes.
segments.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
lines: On their anniversary, Cliff rowed Darlene out at sunset.
Five minutes later, they were arguing about which way was left.
Darlene laughed. Robert Louis Stevenson had it right:
Marriage is one long conversation, checkered by disputes.
Forty years of it. They rowed in circles, and neither one wanted to go back.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start small. Do the next thing. Ask. Go slow. Try again. Keep talking.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start small. Do what's in front of you. Ask for help. Go slow. Try again. Keep talking.
I tried rowing once. I went backwards for an hour and called it a cruise.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
